## Prediction, exploration and explanation

**Predict (1–2 minutes).** Assign the changing carbon in ethanol before checking. Use +1 per C–O bond order, −1 per C–H bond and 0 per C–C bond. Is your answer a formal charge?

**Explore (3–4 minutes).** Check ethanol, then use the selected-next-oxidation button to move through ethanal to ethanoic acid. Compare propan-2-ol with propanone. Finally inspect 2-methylpropan-2-ol and explain why the simple next-oxidation button is unavailable.

**Explain (2 minutes).** Show one full bond-count calculation. Why can oxidation happen without adding a new oxygen atom? Why would retaining all three C–C bonds while converting the tertiary centre to C=O give an invalid ordinary carbon?

## Supplied model and its limits

The displayed value is the **oxidation state of the changing carbon**, not its formal charge. C–O bond order contributes +1, C–H −1, C–C 0. The supplied selected net maps are primary alcohol→aldehyde→acid and secondary alcohol→ketone. The tertiary centre has no attached H, so the simple carbon-skeleton-retaining map cannot be used. Other harsh, C–C-cleaving chemistry is outside this model; no laboratory conditions are supplied.

## Carry the explanation into practice

Return to the local [alcohols redox lesson](../alcohols-redox/exercise.qmd). Keep your prediction, a corrected drawing or calculation, and two sentences stating what the model supports and what it leaves unresolved. The interactive works locally and needs no online account or additional software packages.
